# Kill matrix

*Generated by `scripts/run_kill_matrix.py`. Do not edit by hand.*

A passing test suite proves nothing on its own -- it might be asserting real
invariants or it might be asserting that `200 == 200`, and from the outside those
look the same. So the mock is booted with one deliberate defect at a time and the
suite is run against it unchanged. A mutant that survives is a documented
behaviour nothing defends.

**18 of 18 mutants killed.**

| `M2` | B-040 | metadata.pending_changes renamed to metadata.changes | `test_a_review_turn_pauses_with_proposals` |

Tests that merely detect *that* a mutant is active -- the posture checks asserting the mock is not secretly running one -- are excluded from these counts. They fail under every mutant, so counting them would make each one look caught even when nothing behavioural noticed.

## Why each defect would matter

**M1 — proposed_change_batch.content arrives already parsed**  
The double-parse asymmetry is the single most warned-about trap in the integration docs. A mock that smooths it over teaches the opposite of what production does.

**M2 — metadata.pending_changes renamed to metadata.changes**  
A review UI reads this key to know what to show; renamed, it renders an empty approval list and the user approves nothing.

**M3 — awaiting_kind omitted from a continue pause**  
Without it the two flavours of awaiting_approval are indistinguishable and a client calls the wrong resume endpoint.

**M4 — approve accepts a batch body with no top-level `approved`**  
The documented 422 is what tells an integrator their batch shape is wrong. Accepting it silently is worse than rejecting it.

**M5 — approve on a continue pause returns 200 instead of 409**  
The 409 is the guard rail that stops a client resolving a pause the wrong way; removing it makes the two paths silently interchangeable.

**M6 — Retry-After dropped from the application 429**  
Clients are told to honour it. Without it they either hammer the service or back off arbitrarily.

**M7 — the infrastructure 429 served as JSON**  
The two 429s need opposite handling -- one means wait for a billing cycle, the other means retry in a second. Made identical, a client cannot choose.

**M8 — the 413 flattened to a bare string detail**  
The structured body is what lets an agent recover automatically instead of surfacing a dead end to a human.

**M9 — limit_expandable flipped to false**  
It reframes a limit that support will raise on request as a hard ceiling, and a client gives up where it should ask.

**M10 — SSE sequence numbers emitted out of order**  
Ordering is what makes resume work at all; out of order, a reconnect silently drops events.

**M11 — last_sequence ignored, full history replayed**  
A resuming client re-processes every event it already handled -- duplicated inserts being the classic symptom.

**M12 — legacy .doc upload returns the documented 415 rather than the real 400**  
Encodes the documentation instead of the behaviour. A mock that matches the docs where the service does not is worse than none.

**M13 — a tool dropped from the advertised MCP surface**  
An agent plans against tools/list. A tool that vanishes turns into a capability the agent believes it lacks.

**M14 — a tool's input argument renamed in its schema**  
Renamed arguments are the quietest possible break: the tool still exists, still runs, and ignores what you pass it.

**M15 — compact response mode returns the full document anyway**  
Compact mode exists to keep large documents out of an agent's context. Ignoring it is a silent cost regression, not a visible failure.

**M16 — an MCP tool error reported with isError false**  
Agents branch on isError. A refusal dressed as a success is acted on.

**M17 — export returns JSON, as the spec wrongly declares**  
Would make the mock agree with the specification and disagree with the service -- exactly the drift this project exists to detect.

**M18 — exporting from an empty session returns an empty document**  
The 404 is what tells an integrator they wired the four calls out of order. An empty file ships to a user instead.

---

Full matrix runs in 105s against the local mock, with no API key and no operations spent.
